name: app.R
content:
source(if (file.exists("teaching.R")) "teaching.R" else "../TeachingTools/teaching.R", local = TRUE)
source("model.R", local = TRUE)

spec <- lesson_spec(
  "Many noisy stars, one population",
  "Infer individual stellar velocities and a shared population mean without pretending that every star is identical.",
  "Partial pooling borrows population information most strongly for the least precisely measured objects.",
  controls = list(
    lesson_choice("pooling", "Inference model", c("Partial pooling" = "partial", "No pooling" = "none", "Complete pooling" = "complete")),
    lesson_slider("scatter", "Intrinsic velocity dispersion (km/s)", 0, 3, 1, 0.1),
    lesson_slider("noise", "Measurement uncertainty multiplier", 0.3, 3, 1, 0.1)
  ),
  lecture = "https://anguswright.github.io/LectureNotes/IntroductionToStatistics_Section4c_html.html",
  section = "4c - Hierarchical Models and Building a Model",
  guide = c("Compare no pooling and partial pooling. Which measurements move most?",
            "Increase observational noise while holding the population dispersion fixed.",
            "Compare complete pooling with a population that really has intrinsic scatter. A simpler model can be too restrictive."),
  explanation = c(
    "Fourteen member-star velocities are drawn from a Normal population with true mean 1.5 km/s. Each star has its own known measurement standard deviation. Membership is known and selection is ignored.",
    "The partial-pooling model is theta_i | mu ~ Normal(mu, tau^2), x_i | theta_i ~ Normal(theta_i, s_i^2), and mu ~ Normal(0, 5^2). The dispersion tau is known in this demonstration. The population mean mu is inferred, and its uncertainty is propagated into every individual interval.",
    "For V = 1/(1/25 + sum[1/(tau^2+s_i^2)]), m = V sum[x_i/(tau^2+s_i^2)], and w_i = tau^2/(tau^2+s_i^2), the individual posterior mean is w_i*x_i + (1-w_i)*m. Its variance is tau^2*s_i^2/(tau^2+s_i^2) + (1-w_i)^2*V.",
    "Complete pooling fits a separate tau=0 model. No pooling uses separate flat individual priors, giving Normal(x_i,s_i^2) posteriors. During animation, positions and interval widths interpolate for illustration; only the final intervals are the stated posterior intervals."
  ),
  presets = list("Precise stars" = list(noise = 0.3, pooling = "partial"),
                 "Uncertain stars" = list(noise = 2.5, pooling = "partial")),
  steps = 60
)
parts <- lesson_components(spec, calculate, draw, measure)
ui <- parts$ui
server <- parts$server
shinyApp(ui, server)

name: model.R
content:
normal_hierarchy <- function(x, error, scatter, prior_mean = 0, prior_sd = 5) {
  variance <- 1 / (1 / prior_sd^2 + sum(1 / (scatter^2 + error^2)))
  mean <- variance * (prior_mean / prior_sd^2 + sum(x / (scatter^2 + error^2)))
  weight <- scatter^2 / (scatter^2 + error^2)
  list(mean = weight * x + (1 - weight) * mean,
       variance = scatter^2 * error^2 / (scatter^2 + error^2) + (1 - weight)^2 * variance,
       population_mean = mean, population_sd = sqrt(variance), weight = weight)
}

calculate <- function(input, phase) {
  truth <- 1.5 + input$scatter * rnorm(14)
  error <- seq(0.25, 1.7, length.out = 14) * input$noise
  observed <- truth + error * rnorm(14)
  posterior <- normal_hierarchy(observed, error, if (input$pooling == "complete") 0 else input$scatter)
  if (input$pooling == "none") {
    posterior$mean <- observed
    posterior$variance <- error^2
  }
  list(truth = truth, error = error, observed = observed, posterior = posterior,
       estimate = observed + phase * (posterior$mean - observed),
       sd = error + phase * (sqrt(posterior$variance) - error))
}

draw <- function(result, input) {
  with(result, {
    extent <- range(observed - 1.96 * error, observed + 1.96 * error, truth,
                    estimate - 1.96 * sd, estimate + 1.96 * sd)
    plot(NA, xlim = extent, ylim = c(0, 16), xlab = "Stellar velocity (km/s)",
         ylab = "", yaxt = "n", main = "Individual estimates, shared information")
    axis(2, at = 1:14, labels = paste("Star", 1:14), las = 1, cex.axis = 0.8)
    abline(v = 1.5, col = lesson_colours["truth"], lty = 2, lwd = 2)
    segments(observed - 1.96 * error, (1:14) + 0.12,
             observed + 1.96 * error, (1:14) + 0.12, col = "#B7C0CF")
    points(observed, (1:14) + 0.12, pch = 1, col = "#7F8A9B")
    segments(estimate - 1.96 * sd, (1:14) - 0.12,
             estimate + 1.96 * sd, (1:14) - 0.12, col = lesson_colours["inference"], lwd = 2)
    points(estimate, (1:14) - 0.12, pch = 16, col = lesson_colours["inference"])
    points(truth, 1:14, pch = 18, col = lesson_colours["truth"])
    legend("top", c("Measured +/- 1.96 SD", "Inferred +/- 1.96 SD", "Truth"),
           col = c("#7F8A9B", lesson_colours["inference"], lesson_colours["truth"]),
           pch = c(1, 16, 18), horiz = TRUE, bty = "n", cex = 0.75)
  })
}

measure <- function(result, input) {
  c("Median individual shift (km/s)" = sprintf("%.2f", median(abs(result$estimate - result$observed))),
    "True population mean (km/s)" = "1.50",
    "Assumed intrinsic dispersion" = if (input$pooling == "complete") "0 (all stars identical)" else if (input$pooling == "none") "Not pooled" else sprintf("%.1f km/s", input$scatter))
}
